output:
**Answer:** Four households are billed in groups that their signed householding agreement contradicts: HH-0586, HH-0592, HH-0928 and HH-4821.

Only these four households have a signed householding agreement. They all follow the same pattern:

- **The agreement:** a three-party letter covering the parents' joint account, one parent's IRA and an adult child's individual account. It says these are "billed together as one group from the next billing cycle."
- **The billing setup:** the portfolio system as of 15 April 2026 still has two groups. The joint account and IRA are in one group, and the child's account is in a separate group on its own.
- **Why it wasn't just pending:** each billing group was last changed in 2021, when the child's account was added. Each agreement was signed later, between October 2023 and November 2024. In every case the "next billing cycle" came before the quarter ending 31 March 2026, so the agreement should already have taken effect.

| Household | Agreement (signed) | Group with joint account and IRA | Child's separate group | Groups last changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0592 Haddad | AGR-0592-3 (2023-10-20) | BG-0592-1 | BG-0592-2 | 2021-09-01 |
| HH-0928 Jablonski | AGR-0928-3 (2024-03-05) | BG-0928-1 | BG-0928-2 | 2021-09-01 |
| HH-0586 Quarshie | AGR-0586-3 (2024-06-07) | BG-0586-1 | BG-0586-2 | 2021-09-01 |
| HH-4821 Okafor-Lind | AGR-4821-3 (2024-11-18) | BG-4821-1 | BG-4821-2 | 2021-09-14 |

**Why it matters:** the fee schedule (FS-STD) is tiered and charged "per billing group." Keeping the child's account in its own group means each household's assets are priced in two smaller pieces instead of one combined total. That can push them into higher fee tiers.

I didn't work out how much each household was overcharged. That would need the quarter-end values, and I only checked the current values. The advisory fees from April 2025 to April 2026 were charged to each account separately at the custodian, which fits the split setup.

Six other households (HH-3058, HH-3462, HH-8312, HH-8865, HH-9234, HH-9571) have advisory agreements that say their accounts are billed together. Each of them is billed as a single group, so there's nothing wrong there.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which households are billed in groups that a signed householding agreement contradicts?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households are, "none_found" if none is, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household that is, each as {"household_id": ..., "agreement_id": the householding agreement, "billing_group_ids": the billing groups that hold its accounts apart, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
